answer: Agents prove unique physical topology by measuring round-trip latency vectors to a rotating grove of beacon nodes; each voyage samples jitter and asymmetric paths that bind identity to a specific distinct network coordinate. The wharf aggregates these signed vectors into a Merkle commitment, so a sybil must replicate the exact multi-homed latency fingerprint -- requiring either colocation with the beacons or expensive BGP manipulation across multiple ASNs -- making mass fabrication cost scale linearly with geographic diversity rather than compute alone.
